about: Research notes come from docs/research/landscape-brief.md and docs/research/verification-results.json (scan of 10 to 12 October 2026). Every note lists its sources.

tools.name: Claude Code (terminal)
tools.research_note: Claude Code has a screen reader mode. You turn it on yourself, because it does not turn on by itself when a screen reader is running. To turn it on, start it with claude --ax-screen-reader, set the environment variable CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1, or add "axScreenReader": true to its settings file. It needs version 2.1.181 or later and was officially released on 20 July 2026. It prints plain labelled lines (you:, claude:, tool:, Permission Required:). It turns menus into numbered lists, and you answer by typing a number. Before you approve changes, it reads them line by line, with plus and minus. It rings the terminal bell when a reply ends or a question waits. Known gap: costs are shown only when you exit. On 17 August 2026 an Anthropic maintainer confirmed that built-in speech, plain-language tool names and heading rules for replies are not shipped.

tools.name: Claude Code for VS Code
tools.research_note: The Claude Code extension for VS Code announces each reply once, when it is complete. This came in version 2.1.236 (19 August 2026), with no setting needed. It also announces permission requests, errors and status changes. Each turn has a hidden heading, so you can jump from turn to turn. Version 2.1.268 added the command Claude Code: Focus last message. A VoiceOver user reported on 28 September 2026 that version 2.1.283 stopped echoing typed characters (issue 97889).

tools.name: Claude Desktop (Code tab)
tools.research_note: Desktop version 1.17377 (21 July 2026) added a heading for each turn. It also announces permission requests without taking focus, and announces when a response starts and ends. Three problems were still open in October 2026. The list of messages in a conversation removes the message your screen reader is reading (issue 99332). With VoiceOver, the file and change panel reads every line as "Add comment" (issue 100911). NVDA users report a silent slash menu, and new replies that are not announced (issues 94353 and 95937). A community script, claude-desktop-stable-feed, keeps every message loaded. You must paste it into the developer console each time you start the app. It was tested on Windows only.

tools.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
tools.research_note: Codex CLI has no dedicated screen reader mode. Since 1 May 2026, the setting tui.animations=false turns every animation off. Since 16 September 2026, Codex checks for a running screen reader when it starts. If it finds one, it saves that setting for you. Version 0.154.0 made VoiceOver read fragments of output until animations were turned off (issue 44728). The request for a --screen-reader flag (issue 20489, 30 April 2026) is still open. In October, a JAWS user still reported repeated speech, and a VoiceOver user could reach only the end of the conversation.

tools.name: Codex desktop app (ChatGPT desktop)
tools.research_note: Screen reader users filed about ten accessibility issues on the Codex desktop app between April and October 2026. The app is now part of the ChatGPT desktop app. Reported problems include focus jumping to the top while it writes (issue 22816). NVDA cannot see the "/" suggestion menu (issue 32375). There are no status announcements (issue 38246). Replies during an active task arrive with no VoiceOver announcement (issue 52784, 10 October 2026). A JAWS user reported in July that most heading problems were fixed. A VoiceOver user on AppleVis called the Mac app the best native experience they had used with VoiceOver, though lacking features. That post's date could not be confirmed.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
tools.research_note: GitHub Copilot CLI has had a --screen-reader mode since October 2025. That was before it became generally available on 25 February 2026. Its new terminal interface became generally available on 23 June 2026. It turns screen reader support on by itself when it detects a screen reader. Its icons are labelled, and its animations switch themselves off. Version 1.0.71 (16 July 2026) announces the focused row in pickers. Version 1.0.81 (27 August 2026) added Ctrl+Space to turn voice dictation on and off. Issue 1642, filed in February by a blind developer, says the status bar is announced on every keypress. The maintainers have not replied to it.

tools.name: VS Code with GitHub Copilot Chat
tools.research_note: VS Code 1.116 (15 April 2026) added landmarks and an accessibility help dialog for the Agents window. You open that dialog with Alt+F1. Version 1.131 (29 July 2026) added experimental built-in offline dictation in chat, editor and terminal. It also added a terminal accessible view that keeps your reading position while output keeps arriving. Version 1.137 added an experimental Voice Mode for talking to an agent. Voice Mode is for individual Copilot plans only. Still open: NVDA stops reading after file dialogs (issue 326546).

tools.name: Cursor
tools.research_note: Cursor 3.23 (early October 2026) lists accessibility fixes. Screen readers announce the highlighted item and its position in the agent input's / and @ menus. Buttons in the agent chat show a focus ring when reached by keyboard. Older forum reports describe the agent panel as "completely opaque" to NVDA and JAWS. The same reports say the editor itself works like VS Code. Their dates could not be confirmed. No Cursor accessibility statement was found. No blind user confirming the 3.23 fixes was found either.

tools.name: Gemini CLI
tools.research_note: Gemini CLI has a plain-text screen reader mode. Start it with --screen-reader, or set ui.accessibility.screenReader to true in its settings. A user on the Antigravity CLI tracker called it "very usable with a screen reader". Its screen reader cursor bug was closed as not planned on 10 May 2026. On 18 June 2026, Gemini CLI stopped serving free, Google AI Pro and Ultra requests, in favour of Antigravity CLI. Paid API keys and Code Assist Standard and Enterprise are not affected.

tools.name: Google Antigravity CLI
tools.research_note: Antigravity CLI has no screen reader mode. It replaced Gemini CLI for free users on 18 June 2026. The request to restore --screen-reader support (issue 6, opened 19 May 2026) is still open. A Google engineer assigned it to themselves on 20 August 2026, with no reply since. A blind VoiceOver user reported they could not get past the first-run setup. Another user called it "impossible for some tasks".

tools.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
tools.research_note: Cognition renamed Windsurf to Devin Desktop on 2 June 2026, and replaced its Cascade agent with Devin Local. Its "Screen Reader Optimized" marketing claim could not be confirmed by any user report, test or documentation. Nothing was found about how the Devin cloud agent works with screen readers.

tools.name: Lovable
tools.research_note: Lovable's accessibility statement aims for WCAG 2.2 level AA, a common standard for web accessibility. It was last updated on 6 August 2026. It is based on an evaluation by Funka between 23 February and 10 July 2026. It is unclear whether it covers the workspace where you build, or only the marketing site. No reports from blind people building with Lovable were found. Nothing comparable was found for Bolt, v0, Base44 or Replit.

sources.title: Lovable accessibility statement

tools.name: OpenCode
tools.research_note: OpenCode has no accessibility mode. An earlier request was closed by a stale bot, which closes quiet requests, on 29 April 2026. Before that, maintainers said they had no capacity. A blind NVDA user made a detailed proposal for a screen_reader setting (issue 39368, 28 July 2026). That proposal is still open. Users report that the desktop app hides streaming text from screen readers. Issue 54652 (12 October 2026) says version 2 still does.

tools.name: BlindPilot
tools.research_note: BlindPilot is an open source desktop app (MIT licence) that runs AI coding agents. It runs Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI, opencode and other agents. It splits each answer into rows you move through with the arrow keys. It has narration modes, permission dialogs and sound cues. It had more than 130 tagged versions between 9 August and 11 October 2026. One person maintains it. The macOS build is not notarized by Apple, and Linux is the least tested. Every agent runs in Bypass permissions mode by default, so the agent does not ask before it acts.

tools.name: agentaloud
tools.research_note: agentaloud is a Windows app, started on 2 September 2026, that runs Claude Code or Codex in the background. It shows the conversation as a read-only transcript. Single-letter keys jump between prompts, answers and tool steps. Each tool step is spoken as one sentence through NVDA. Permission requests appear as dialogs that show the exact command. It needs Windows 10 or 11 and NVDA. In October 2026 it was not known how mature it is.
